# Part 1: Environment isolation

This activity highlights important differences in how `venv` and `conda` create “isolated” environments.

:::{.card .border-primary .mb-3}
:::{.card-header}
## Getting Started
:::
:::{.card-body}

#### 1. Record the path to your base `python3` executable

Use `command` and `realpath` to expose the source of your base `python3` executable.  
Record this path in the box below for future reference.

```bash
realpath "$(command -v python3)"
```

<span class="text-primary">Record path below:</span>
<div class="textbox textbox-editable" contenteditable="true"></div>

:::
:::


:::{.card .border-primary .mb-3}
:::{.card-header}
## Venv
:::
:::{.card-body}

#### 2. Create and activate a new `venv` environment

Create a new `venv` environment called `test_env_1`:

```bash
python3 -m venv test_env_1
```

Activate your new environment:

```bash
source test_env_1/bin/activate
```

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
You can revert to a clean state at any time with:  
`deactivate; rm -rf test_env_1/`
:::

#### 3. Determine the location of your Python executable in `test_env_1`

```bash
realpath "$(command -v python3)"
```

<span class="text-primary">Record path below:</span>
<div class="textbox textbox-editable" contenteditable="true"></div>

**3.1 Is this the same as your base `python3` path?**

:::


:::{.card .border-primary .mb-3}
:::{.card-header}
## Conda / Mamba
:::
:::{.card-body}

#### 4. Create and activate a new conda environment

Create a new conda environment called `test_env_1`:

```bash
conda create -n test_env_1 python
```

Activate your new environment:

```bash
conda activate test_env_1
```

#### 5. Determine the location of your Python executable again

```bash
realpath "$(command -v python3)"
```

# Part 2: Silent Changes

This section shows how `pip` can silently alter already-installed packages to satisfy new requirements, potentially breaking existing workflows. Then you will repeat the same setup using `conda`.

:::{.callout-note appearance="simple"}
Attempt each step below before exposing the answer
:::

:::{.card .border-secondary .mb-3}
:::{.card-header}
## Part 2A: Business as usual (`venv`)
:::
:::{.card-body}

#### 1. Download the test script and dataset
This activity will use a simple python script that reads in two CSV files and joins them together using `pandas`.

Use the commands below to download the Python script and CSV files.
```bash
wget https://github.com/DOH-JDJ0303/binfx-hub/raw/refs/heads/main/docs/presentations/2026/International_Influenza_Workshop/pt2_script.py -O pt2_script.py
wget https://github.com/DOH-JDJ0303/binfx-hub/raw/refs/heads/main/docs/presentations/2026/International_Influenza_Workshop/pt2_data_1.csv -O pt2_data_1.csv
wget https://github.com/DOH-JDJ0303/binfx-hub/raw/refs/heads/main/docs/presentations/2026/International_Influenza_Workshop/pt2_data_2.csv -O pt2_data_2.csv
```

#### 2. Create and activate a new `venv` environment

Use `venv` create and activate new environment called `test_env_2`.

:::{.callout-tip collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
## Answer
```bash
python3 -m venv test_env_2
source test_env_2/bin/activate
```
:::

#### 3. Install pinned dependencies

The Python script requires `pandas` v1.5.0, which requires a `numpy` version < 2. Install these in your `test_env_2` environment.

:::{.callout-tip collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
## Answer
```bash
pip install --upgrade pip "numpy<2.0" "pandas==1.5.0"
```
:::

#### 4. Run the test script
Run the script you downloaded in step 1.

```bash
python3 ./pt2_script.py
```

If successful, it should print out a summary of three dataframes: `Dataframe 1`, `Dataframe 2`, and `Combined Dataframes`

**Did the script work?**

<div class="btn-group" role="group">
  <input type="radio" class="btn-check" name="venv-radio2" id="venv2-yes" autocomplete="off">
  <label class="btn btn-outline-primary" for="venv2-yes">Yes</label>

  <input type="radio" class="btn-check" name="venv-radio2" id="venv2-no" autocomplete="off">
  <label class="btn btn-outline-primary" for="venv2-no">No</label>
</div>

:::
:::

:::{.card .border-secondary .mb-3}
:::{.card-header}
## Part 2A: The disruption
:::
:::{.card-body}

#### 5. Install scanpy with pip
One of the other bioinformaticians in your lab is having trouble installing the Python module, `scanpy`. They ask if you are able to install it on your machine.

:::{.callout-tip collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
## Answer
```bash
pip install scanpy
```
:::

#### 6. Back to your test script

With that out of the way, you get back to running your test script.
```bash
python3 pt2_script.py
```

**Did the script work?**

<div class="btn-group" role="group">
  <input type="radio" class="btn-check" name="venv-radio3" id="venv3-yes" autocomplete="off">
  <label class="btn btn-outline-primary" for="venv3-yes">Yes</label>

  <input type="radio" class="btn-check" name="venv-radio3" id="venv3-no" autocomplete="off">
  <label class="btn btn-outline-primary" for="venv3-no">No</label>
</div>

**If not, why?**

<span class="text-primary">Record notes below:</span>
<div class="textbox textbox-editable" contenteditable="true"></div>

:::{.callout-tip collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
## Answer
Check your `pandas` version using `pip list | grep pandas`. Does this match the `v1.5.0` you installed in step 3?
:::

:::
:::

:::{.card .border-secondary .mb-3}
:::{.card-header}
## Part 2B: Business as usual (`conda`)
:::
:::{.card-body}

#### 1. Create and activate a new conda environment

Use `conda` to create and activate a new environment called `test_env_2`

:::{.callout-tip collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
## Answer
```bash
conda create -n test_env_2 python=3.10 -y
conda activate test_env_2
```
:::

#### 2. Install the pinned dependencies with conda

Install the same dependencies as before (`pandas` v1.5.0 and `numpy` < v2.0), but with `conda`.

:::{.callout-tip collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
## Answer
```bash
conda install -y -c conda-forge "numpy<2.0" "pandas=1.5.0"
```
:::

#### 3. Run the test script:

```bash
python3 ./pt2_script.py
```

**Did the script work?**

<div class="btn-group" role="group">
  <input type="radio" class="btn-check" name="conda-radio2" id="conda2-yes" autocomplete="off">
  <label class="btn btn-outline-primary" for="conda2-yes">Yes</label>

  <input type="radio" class="btn-check" name="conda-radio2" id="conda2-no" autocomplete="off">
  <label class="btn btn-outline-primary" for="conda2-no">No</label>
</div>

#### 4. Install scanpy with Conda
Use conda to install `scanpy` and confirm `[Y]` / deny `[n]` the changes based on the summary.

:::{.callout-tip collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
## Answer
```bash
conda install -c conda-forge -c bioconda scanpy
```
:::

<span class="text-primary"> Which did you choose - `Y` or `n`? Why?</span>
<div class="textbox textbox-editable" contenteditable="true"></div>

#### 5. Run the test script:
Try the test script one time after making your decision.

```bash
python3 ./pt2_script.py
```

**Did the script work?**

  <input type="radio" class="btn-check" name="conda-radio3" id="conda3-yes" autocomplete="off">
  <label class="btn btn-outline-primary" for="conda3-yes">Yes</label>

  <input type="radio" class="btn-check" name="conda-radio3" id="conda3-no" autocomplete="off">
  <label class="btn btn-outline-primary" for="conda3-no">No</label>
</div>

**Do you regret your decision?**

<div class="btn-group" role="group">
  <input type="radio" class="btn-check" name="conda-radio4" id="conda4-yes" autocomplete="off">
  <label class="btn btn-outline-primary" for="conda4-yes">Yes</label>

  <input type="radio" class="btn-check" name="conda-radio4" id="conda4-no" autocomplete="off">
  <label class="btn btn-outline-primary" for="conda4-no">No</label>
</div>

:::{.callout-tip collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
## Answer
Conda warned us that installing `scanpy` would require updating to a new version of `pandas`. This allowed us to avoid silently breaking the `pandas v1.5.0` dependency of `pt2_script.py`.
:::
